question: Will the US conduct a new military strike inside Iranian territory between October 15 and October 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: an operational lull; by Oct 2 a tracker reported 25 days with no US strike ashore. Since the September 1 waves, no qualifying hits on Iranian land, islands or territorial waters are documented; the Sept 8 tanker and Sept 14 boat strikes are not clearly inside 12nm. Trump has signalled renewed strikes after the Nov 3 midterms, so the Oct 15-16 window falls in a pre-election restraint period. Upside risks: strikes came in clusters in July and September, small self-defense strikes happen ad hoc (Larak Island, Aug 30), Iran keeps the Strait closed and tankers were hit Oct 3-4, and a third carrier arrives. Base rate for a 2-day window during the lull is roughly 0-8%. Market check: Polymarket 'US-Iran ceasefire continues through...?' prices Oct 5 at 99% and Oct 7 at 97% ($6M volume) but has no Oct 15-16 date and its rules were not checked; 'US strikes Iran by...?' is already resolved; Kalshi and bookmakers not checked.

- Status quo: no US strikes on Iranian territory since early September. The iranwarlive.com daily recap for Oct 2 says 'No US strike ashore for a 25th period'; the Oct 1, 3 and 4 entries report no strike.
- Aug 30 2026: US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island after seeing preparations to lay sea mines (Wikipedia, September 2026 US strikes on Iran).
- Sep 1 2026: two US waves on southern Iran (Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, Jask, Sirik, Konarak, Asaluyeh, Ahvaz) after IRGC attacks on shipping and on US forces (CENTCOM via CNBC/Wikipedia).
- Sep 5-9 2026: US struck five IRGC-linked oil tankers after an IRGC missile attempt on a US warship. These are vessel strikes and may lie outside 12nm (NPR, Al Jazeera).
- Sep 14 2026: a US drone reportedly fired two missiles at two IRGC small boats trying to seize a US unmanned vessel; location relative to 12nm not established.
- July 2026: CENTCOM ran 13 straight nights of strikes (July 11-23), so active phases bring daily strikes.
- Oct 1 2026 (Washington Times, Time interview): Trump says strikes could resume after the Nov 3 midterms if no deal; reports say he rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan.
- Oct 2-4 2026 (CBS, Al Jazeera, Fox): Camp David meeting of senior officials with no announced outcome; Iran says Hormuz stays closed; tankers hit by unknown projectiles on Oct 3 and 4; Hegseth calls the US blockade 'ironclad' and says all options are on the table.
- A third carrier strike group (Theodore Roosevelt) plus the Makin Island amphibious group is arriving, with US naval presence over 20,000 by end of October (globalsecurity.org search snippet).
- Event-in-window count: in the ~25 days from about Sep 10 to Oct 5, no documented US strike ashore in Iran. Two-day windows with a qualifying strike: about 0 of 12, apart from the possible Sep 14 boat strike if it was within 12nm. In the Aug 30 - Sep 9 escalation, most two-day windows had one.
- Markets: Polymarket has a 'US-Iran ceasefire continues through...?' market (dates Oct 5 and Oct 7 seen, about $6M volume), rules not checked. No market found for this two-day window. Kalshi and bookmakers not checked.
- Searched without finding: any CENTCOM release after mid-September on strikes in Iran; Polymarket ceasefire market rules; exact coordinates of the Sep 14 boat strike.

calls.reference_class: 2-day windows during the post-Sept-1-2026 operational lull in the US-Iran war, counting US strikes on Iranian land or territorial waters

calls.reasoning: As of Oct 3-4, a tracker reported 26 consecutive operational periods without a US strike on Iranian soil. The last confirmed strikes ashore were Aug 30 (Larak Island) and Sep 1. US officials report that Trump has tied renewed bombing to after the Nov 3 midterms, so Oct 15-16 falls inside a period of stated restraint. In the current lull, a 2-day window that contains a qualifying strike looks like roughly 2-8%. The upside comes from reactive retaliation. The Jul 29 and Sep 1 waves came the same day or the next day after IRGC fire on US forces. Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping continue, and naval clashes in the Strait could fall inside Iran's 12nm waters. Attacks on commercial shipping alone have not triggered strikes ashore since early September.
calls.reconciliation: No web access on this run. All three runs found the same status quo: no US strike ashore since early September, 25-26 tracker periods with no strike up to Oct 3, and Trump signalling strikes after the midterms. The factual disputes are minor. (1) Whether the Sep 14/15 drone strike on IRGC boats happened inside 12nm: no run could establish this, so it stays uncertain. It matters only because Strait engagements could qualify, and I give that path a small share of the probability. (2) When the third carrier arrives (end of October vs November): either way it is after or barely around the window, so the effect is small. (3) Whether the Sep 5 tanker strikes count: probably not, given the 12nm rule. It does not change the lull picture. The remaining differences are judgment calls about the per-day hazard during the lull. Stated restraint and a month without strikes ashore pull toward the low end. Continuing IRGC attacks on shipping and the US pattern of fast reactive strikes keep a real tail. My estimate is 6%. No human market matching the Oct 15-16 window was reported. The Polymarket ceasefire market the runs mention is a near-miss contract, not an anchor.
